page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DLDSv5 server family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this server features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration includes a 3686 GB local SSD for high-speed storage and supports Premium Storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25% tier. The system demonstrates high memory bandwidth, achieving 5005.65 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 328.17 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. It also exhibits strong performance in database operations, Redis SET operations at 88.36 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 64.98 GB/sec. Single-core performance, including single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, falls within the average middle 50% tier.

Due to its low memory-to-CPU ratio, the D96lds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-intensive workloads that do not require massive RAM allocations. The combination of 96 dedicated vCPUs and a large 3686 GB local SSD makes it highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, web serving, and high-throughput data processing. However, memory-bound applications requiring more than 2.0 GB of RAM per core may experience resource constraints.
